alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Glycogen granules are highly electron-dense structures in the cytoplasm. They readily aggregate into clusters, as seen in this liver cell and would stain positively with the periodic-Schiff stain (PAS) by light microscopy. Glycogen granules are not surrounded by a membrane.

Secretory granules can vary in their staining properties, depending on the contents of the granules.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Mitochondria are composed of an inner and an outer membrane, the inner membrane has shelf-like or tubular folds called cristae. Mitochondrial shape and size can be highly variable and reflects the metabolic requirements of the cell. It is estimated that each liver cell (seen here) has over 800 mitochondria.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Polysomes, or polyribosomes, are clusters of ribosomes arranged as circles or spirals, which are threaded onto a single messenger RNA molecule (not resolved in this image). Ribosomes are electron dense and approximately one-fourth the size of glycogen granules. Proteins synthesized on polysomes are used within the cell.

alternativas.feedback: The nuclear envelope is composed of two unit membranes, the inner and outer nuclear membranes enclosing a perinuclear space. The outer membrane is continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum and often possesses ribosomes on its cytoplasmic surface. The nuclear envelope is not continuous; it is interrupted by nuclear pores allowing bidirectional transport between the nucleus and cytoplasm.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Chromatin is a complex of protein and DNA within the nucleus. Heteochromatin is electron dense and transcriptionally less active than the more electron lucent, euchromatin which is transcriptionally active. Heterochromatin is frequently distributed in a perinuclear distribution immediately beneath the nuclear envelope.

alternativas.feedback: The diplosome consists of two centrioles at right angles to each other. During S phase of the cell cycle, the centrioles of the diplosome duplicate, forming two diplosomes which migrate to opposite sides of the nucleus during prophase. The diplosomes produce the mitotic spindle.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum, well developed in this steroid-secreting cell, consists of a membranous network of tubules lacking ribosomes. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is distinguished from the Golgi, which also has smooth membranes, but is organized as stacks of cisternae. SER is the major site of lipid and cholesterol synthesis.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Microtubules are the hollow only cytoskeletal element, shaped like a soda straw. They provide a network within the cell for intracellular transport. In dividing cells, microtubules form the mitotic spindle. In addition, microtubules form aggregate structures, centrioles, basal bodies and the axoneme of cilia and flagella.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Lysosomes are organelles that contain hydrolytic enzymes and are surrounded by a single membrane. The contents of a lysosome can appear highly heterogeneous depending on the type of material that is being broken down. Lysosomes form by the fusion of Golgi-derived, pre-lysosomal vesicles with either internalized materials or autophagosomes.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The nucleolus is highly basophilic and is located within the nucleus. The nucleolus stains heavily with hematoxylin due to its large quantity of DNA and RNA. It appears smooth and spherical, though not surrounded by a membrane. Heterochromatin is also basophilic, but is distributed throughout the nucleus and varies in size. The paler-blue region surrounding the nucleolus is the highly euchromatic nucleus.
